title: Adobe Blog, “Brutalist Web Designers Eschew Rules for UX Best Practices”
lede: An early trade article that credits Pascal Deville with codifying brutalist web design and quotes his reasons.
summary: Adobe’s 2016 article on the brutalist web movement, with quotes from Pascal Deville of brutalistwebsites.com.

evidence.note: Article text read on 2026-10-02. The date comes from the URL path (2016/12/01). No byline was found in the extracted text. The embedded animation was not inspected.

styles.note: Dated attestation of the name and of Deville’s role. Partial fit: it describes both the plain and the deliberately difficult branches.

context: “One of the first people to codify brutalist web design was Pascal Deville,” creative director at Freundliche Grüsse and founder of [Brutalist Websites](ref:brutalist-websites-directory).

Deville: many designers explain it “as a kind of a minimalist movement. They want to get rid of all the creative elements and stuff you can add to a website today.” Others come from punk or hardcore culture, “where things are very rough”.
Deville also calls it a push against UX design that “has become a style that is very dominated by how Google and Apple do stuff”.
The article frames brutalist sites as “rougher, more basic — and at the same time more difficult to navigate”, which mixes in the antidesign branch.
interpretation: Good for dating and for motive. Its description of difficulty belongs to antidesign, which [NN/g (2017)](ref:nngroup-brutalism-antidesign-article-2017) later separated.
